question: The number of neutrons in an oxygen atom is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**8**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Atomic Number** of **Oxygen** is **8**, which indicates that a neutral atom of oxygen contains **8 protons** in its nucleus and **8 electrons** orbiting the nucleus.
 
• The **Mass Number** (atomic mass) of the most common and stable isotope of **Oxygen** (Oxygen-16) is approximately **16**.
 
• To find the **number of neutrons**, the formula used is: **Number of Neutrons = Mass Number (A) - Atomic Number (Z)**. For **Oxygen-16**, this calculation is **16 - 8 = 8**. ***Hence, the statement that oxygen has 8 neutrons is correct.***
 
• While **Oxygen** has three stable isotopes, **Oxygen-16** is the most abundant, making up about **99.76%** of natural oxygen found on Earth.
 
• The electronic configuration of an **Oxygen** atom is **1s² 2s² 2p⁴**, showing that it has **6 valence electrons** in its outermost shell.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chemical Properties of Oxygen:**

 
 
• **Oxygen** is a highly reactive **non-metal** and an **oxidizing agent** that readily forms **oxides** with most elements.
 
• It belongs to **Group 16** (the **chalcogens**) and **Period 2** of the **Periodic Table**.
 
• In its standard form, it is a **diatomic gas** with the formula **O₂**, which is **colorless**, **odorless**, and **tasteless**.
 
 
 
• **Isotopes of Oxygen:**
 
 
• **Oxygen-17**: Contains **8 protons** and **9 neutrons**, with a natural abundance of **0.038%**.
 
• **Oxygen-18**: Contains **8 protons** and **10 neutrons**, with a natural abundance of **0.205%**.
 
• These isotopes are often used in **paleoclimatology** to determine historical **global temperatures** and **ice volume**.
 
 
 
• **Biological and Environmental Importance:**
 
 
• **Oxygen** constitutes approximately **21%** of the Earth's **atmosphere** by volume.
 
• It is essential for **aerobic respiration** in almost all living organisms and is produced during **photosynthesis** by plants and algae.
 
• **Ozone (O₃)** is an allotrope of oxygen located in the **stratosphere** that protects the Earth from harmful **ultraviolet (UV) radiation**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Discovery:** **Oxygen** was first discovered by **Carl Wilhelm Scheele** in **1772**, but **Joseph Priestley** is often credited with the discovery as he published his findings first in **1774**. The name "Oxygen" was coined by **Antoine Lavoisier** in **1777**.
 
• **Abundance:** It is the **third most abundant element** in the universe by mass, after **hydrogen** and **helium**, and the **most abundant element** by mass in the **Earth's crust** (making up about **46.6%**).
 
• **Valency:** **Oxygen** typically has a **valency of 2**, as it requires two electrons to complete its **octet** in the outer shell, leading to its characteristic **-2 oxidation state** in most compounds.
 
• **Liquid Oxygen:** At very low temperatures (below **-183°C** or **90 K**), oxygen condenses into a **pale blue liquid** which is strongly **paramagnetic**.
